name: Vedic recitation (vedapāṭha, svādhyāya of the Saṃhitā)
method_summary: Learning and reciting one's śākhā's Saṃhitā orally from the teacher's mouth, phrase by phrase, with exact accents marked by hand movements, first in the continuous form, then word by word and in the interwoven recitations; daily recitation of the Veda is itself counted a sacrifice (brahmayajña). The Soma book says whoever studies the purifying verses eats purified food (RV 9.67.31).
prerequisites: upanayana (initiation) by a teacher of the śākhā
duration: years of daily study; the complete Saṃhitā with its modified recitations traditionally takes a decade or more (as reported; low confidence)
signs_of_progress: mastery of the Saṃhitā, then pada, krama and the vikṛtis
the six virtues of a reciter (sweetness, distinctness, word-division, accent, composure, tempo)

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
One who recites the Veda without understanding its meaning is a post bearing a load; what is repeated without understanding never blazes, like dry fuel without fire.
Studying without the hand-gestures, lacking accent and letters, one is 'burned' by the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman.

name: Word-by-word recitation (padapāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting the Saṃhitā word by word, with sandhi undone and compound members marked, as fixed in the Padapāṭha ascribed to Śākalya.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.

name: Step recitation (kramapāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting overlapping pairs of words (ab, bc, cd …) so that both the words and their junctions are fixed; taught in the Prātiśākhyas.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.

name: Braid recitation (jaṭāpāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting each pair forward, backward and forward again (ab ba ab, bc cb bc …).

name: Dense recitation (ghanapāṭha)
method_summary: The most elaborate commonly practised recitation (ab ba abc cba abc, bc cb bcd dcb bcd …), whose master is called ghanapāṭhin.

name: The eight modified recitations (vikṛti)
method_summary: Jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha and ghana: permutations built on the krama that lock the order of every word of the text.
notes: List as traditionally given; the source ascription is low-confidence.

name: Sāman chanting (sāmagāna)
method_summary: Singing the verses of the Sāmaveda to their melodies as given in the song-books — village and forest songs and their ritual applications — with stretched vowels, repetitions and stobhas, the notes shown on the fingers; at the soma rite the udgātṛ, prastotṛ and pratihartṛ divide the parts.

warnings.text: A mantra wrong in accent or letter does not convey its meaning; as a verbal thunderbolt it harms the sacrificer, as 'Indra-śatru' did through a fault of accent.
The forest (āraṇyageya) melodies are regarded as potent and are learned apart, outside the village (as reported).

name: Repetition of the Gāyatrī (Sāvitrī)
method_summary: Repeating the Sāvitrī verse to Savitṛ ('we meditate on that excellent radiance … may he impel our thoughts'), preceded by Oṃ and bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, at the twilights; it is imparted by the teacher at initiation.
prerequisites: initiation (upanayana) in the tradition's own rules
notes: The rules of who may recite it and how often belong to the gṛhya and dharma literature (U02).

name: Twilight worship (sandhyāvandana)
method_summary: The daily worship at the junctions of the day by the initiated: purification with water, the sin-effacing verses (RV 10.190), offerings of water to the sun, and repetition of the Gāyatrī.
notes: U01 contribution: its Saṃhitā mantras. The rite's structure is set out in gṛhya/dharma texts (U02).

name: Aghamarṣaṇa (the sin-effacing recitation)
method_summary: Reciting RV 10.190 ('ṛta and satya were born from kindled tapas …') while immersed in water or holding water, to efface sin, at the bath and in the twilight worship.

name: Repetition of the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya (Tryambaka) verse
method_summary: Repeating and offering with the verse 'we worship Tryambaka … may I be freed from death, not from immortality' for release from death and for health; in the Yajurveda it accompanies the Tryambaka offerings to Rudra.

name: Recitation of the Śatarudrīya with the Camaka (Rudra-japa)
method_summary: Chanting the Namaka (homage to Rudra in all forms) with the Camaka (petitions 'for me'), singly or in multiples — traditionally eleven recitations (ekādaśa-rudra), 121 (laghu-rudra), 1,331 (mahā-rudra), 14,641 (ati-rudra); in the agnicayana the Śatarudrīya pacifies Rudra.
notes: The multiples are recalled from living practice literature (moderate confidence).

name: Rudrābhiṣeka (bathing the liṅga with the Rudram)
method_summary: Bathing an image or liṅga of Śiva with water, milk and other substances while the Śatarudrīya is chanted — a later temple and domestic worship that employs the Saṃhitā litany.
notes: Post-Saṃhitā usage (Āgamic/Purāṇic setting); only the Vedic mantra element is U01's.

name: Peace chants (śānti-pāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting peace invocations at the beginning and end of study and rites: 'may we hear with our ears what is auspicious' (RV 1.89.8), 'may Mitra be propitious to us' (1.90.9), 'peace be heaven, peace the atmosphere …' (VS 36.17), 'peaceful be heaven, peaceful the earth' (AVŚ 19.9).

name: Rites for retentive wisdom (medhājanana)
method_summary: Invoking Vācaspati and Medhā for the strength to retain the Veda — AVŚ 1.1 ('may Vācaspati place in me today the strengths of the thrice-seven') and 6.108 — at the start of study.

name: Riddle exchange (brahmodya)
method_summary: A ritual exchange of riddles about the cosmos between priests (e.g. at the horse sacrifice: 'who moves alone?' — 'the sun moves alone'), testing and displaying knowledge of hidden correspondences.

name: The śrauta sacrifice (in general)
method_summary: Solemn rites performed in three fires (gārhapatya, āhavanīya, dakṣiṇāgni) by priests of the Vedas — hotṛ (Ṛgveda), adhvaryu (Yajurveda), udgātṛ (Sāmaveda) and brahmán (overseer), up to sixteen in the great soma rites — for a patron (yajamāna) and his wife, with oblations, recitations, chants and gifts (dakṣiṇā).
prerequisites: initiated householder, married, who has established the fires

name: Establishing the sacred fires (agnyādhāna)
method_summary: The rite by which a householder establishes the three śrauta fires, after which the daily and seasonal offerings become his lifelong duty.

name: The daily fire offering (agnihotra)
method_summary: Offering milk into the fire at sunrise and sunset, daily for life, by one who has established the fires.

name: New- and full-moon offerings (darśapūrṇamāsa)
method_summary: The fortnightly offerings of cakes and other substances at new and full moon, the model (prakṛti) of all iṣṭi rites; the White Yajurveda begins with its formulas.

name: The seasonal rites (cāturmāsya)
method_summary: Offerings at the beginning of the three four-month seasons, including the Sākamedha with the Tryambaka offerings to Rudra.

name: The animal sacrifice (paśubandha)
method_summary: The offering of an animal bound to the sacrificial post (yūpa); recorded as a summary only.

warnings.text: The Vedic verses ask that the victim 'not die but go to the gods by easy paths'; later traditions (Upaniṣadic, Jain, Buddhist, Vaiṣṇava) criticize or replace animal offerings.

name: The soma sacrifice (agniṣṭoma)
method_summary: The paradigm soma rite: the consecrated sacrificer buys the soma, which is pressed three times in one day, offered and drunk, with the chanting of the stotras by the udgātṛs and the recitation of the śastras by the hotṛs.

name: Vājapeya
method_summary: A soma rite of 'the drink of strength', with a chariot race, granting pre-eminence.

name: Royal consecration (rājasūya)
method_summary: The soma rite consecrating a king, with the royal anointing and symbolic acts of sovereignty.

name: Building the fire altar (agnicayana)
method_summary: The great rite of piling a bird-shaped fire altar of bricks in layers, opened by the verses on yoking the mind (VS 11.1–5 = TS 4.1.1), with the Śatarudrīya to appease Rudra and the Camaka at the stream of ghee; its meaning is expounded in the Brāhmaṇas.

name: Horse sacrifice (aśvamedha)
method_summary: The royal rite in which a horse wanders for a year and is then sacrificed, with riddle exchanges and prayers for the realm; recorded as a summary only.

name: Sautrāmaṇī
method_summary: A rite to Indra the good protector (sutrāman) with offerings including surā, performed for healing and restoration.

name: Pravargya
method_summary: The secret rite of the heated pot (gharma) of milk, taught in the forest; its mantras stand in the last books of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā and in the Āraṇyakas.

name: Consecration of the sacrificer (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The consecration before the soma rite: the sacrificer is shaved, bathed, clothed anew, restricted in food and speech and kept apart, and so 'reborn' fit for the gods; 'here I go from untruth to truth' (VS 1.5) is the vow-taker's formula.

warnings.text: The dietary restrictions of the consecration are ritual observances within the rite; they are not recorded here in detail.

name: Vedic funeral (pitṛmedha / antyeṣṭi as the hymns give it)
method_summary: Cremation or burial with the funeral hymns: the corpse on the pyre is sent to the fathers with Agni asked to carry, not consume, it; the flesh-eating fire is sent away; the widow rises from beside the dead; the living set a boundary against death; the bones are laid in the earth; the fathers are invited to the offerings.

equivalents.note: The Saṃhitā hymns supply the mantras of the later gṛhya funeral (antyeṣṭi); the procedures are fixed in the sūtras.

name: Offering to the fathers (piṇḍapitṛyajña)
method_summary: Offering rice-balls and water to the three generations of fathers, who are called to come with svadhā.

name: Tapas (austerity, generative heat)
method_summary: Ascetic exertion that 'heats' the practitioner: by it the ancients reached heaven, the seers were born, the student fills the worlds; the Vrātya stands upright for a year; the unheated cannot attain soma.

warnings.text: Lopāmudrā's complaint that many autumns of toil wear away the body, and the resolution that tapas and married life together bear fruit, are the Saṃhitā's own counterweight to one-sided austerity.

notes: Extreme austerities are not described in method; none of the Saṃhitā passages gives steps.

name: Vedic studentship (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Living with the teacher after initiation, tending his fire with fuel, wearing the girdle and antelope skin, begging, studying the Veda, in chastity and toil (AVŚ 11.5).
notes: U01 contribution: the Atharvavedic studentship. Other units contribute brahmacarya as celibacy (yama).

name: Silence of the muni (mauna, mauneya)
method_summary: The state of the silent sage who, 'ecstatic with munihood', is carried by the winds while others see only his body (RV 10.136.3).
notes: The Keśin hymn describes the state, not a method.

name: Giving (dāna, dakṣiṇā)
method_summary: Giving food and wealth to the needy, the friend and the priest; the gift at the sacrifice (dakṣiṇā).

warnings.text: Who eats alone has only sin; the wealth of the non-giver finds no one to pity him.

name: Honouring the guest (atithi-satkāra)
method_summary: Receiving a guest with water, seat and food, which the Atharvaveda equates point by point with performing the sacrifice; the Vrātya who knows is to be honoured above oneself.

name: Atharvavedic healing rites (bhaiṣajya)
method_summary: Healing by recitation of the hymns with plants, water, amulets, fire and the sun, touching the patient, and sending the disease away to distant places or creatures (fever, jaundice, leprosy, worms, consumption).
notes: Summary only; the Kauśika Sūtra gives the rite details (U02).

name: Binding amulets (maṇi)
method_summary: Binding on an amulet of plant, wood or other substance with Atharvavedic verses for protection, health, victory or prosperity.

name: Rites for long life (āyuṣya)
method_summary: Recitations and rites to hold back death and restore life-breath, keeping the person 'in the world of the living' (AVŚ 8.1).

name: Rites for concord (sāṃmanasya)
method_summary: Rites with the concord hymns to make family and assembly of one heart and mind.

name: Pacificatory rites (śānti)
method_summary: Rites appeasing portents, planets and harmful powers with the peace hymns.

name: Hostile rites (abhicāra) and their counter-rites
method_summary: The Atharvaveda contains spells against rivals and sorcerers and counter-spells returning a harmful spell (kṛtyā) to its sender; recorded here as a category only, without procedure.

warnings.text: Mīmāṃsā's standard example: the Veda describes the śyena rite for harming an enemy, yet such harm is not dharma — the rite is described, not commended (Śabara on Mīmāṃsā Sūtra 1.1.2, recalled with moderate confidence).
Vasiṣṭha's oath 'may I die today if I am a sorcerer' shows the gravity of the charge of sorcery.

notes: Summary only by design (treated as restricted: harmful rites; no procedure recorded).
